transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-19
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Raj Patel (BeaconForge VP Eng), Elena Morozova (BeaconForge Head of ML), Tom Nguyen (BeaconForge Infra Lead), Priya Suresh (BeaconForge Product)

Auto-summary (auto-generated):
- Check-in on renewal timeline and proposed capacity uplift for Q2-Q3; primary ask is EU region + reserved capacity bump.
- Discussed hosted vs dedicated vs VPC (private) tradeoffs; customer leaning toward Dedicated + EU VPC for residency.
- Agreed next steps: pricing + SOW, benchmarking window, and data handoff for traffic profiles.

Topics: renewal timeline, EU VPC onboarding, capacity sizing, latency SLOs, security & KMS, benchmark plan, rollout plan

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): hey everyone thanks for joining on short notice uh we'll give a quick agenda 1) renewal ask and numbers 2) eu onboarding plan 3) benchmarks 4) next steps does that sound ok to you all
[00:12] Raj (BeaconForge): sounds good, maya, thanks. we only have about an hour so maybe keep the details on the infra side for diego and tom to dig into.
[00:20] Maya: perfect. quick context for anyone new: BeaconForge's contract is up end of April. they're asking for a 2x capacity bump and EU region plus private VPC for data residency. this call is to align on timeline and what we need to deliver to get a signed amendment.
[00:39] Tom (BeaconForge): yep that's right. Q2 ramp target is mid-May for early customers in eu. latency target is p95 <= 180ms for chat generation across our prompt mixes.
[00:50] Diego (Redwood SE): okay got it. do you have current baseline numbers for p95 and qps? even ballpark helps for sizing.
[00:58] Raj: sure um our production 7-day peak is around 1,200 qps (average token length ~45), p95 on current hosted setup is about 210ms with occasional spikes. we want headroom for 2x so planning for 2,500 qps peak.
[01:14] Maya: nice detail. so you're asking for reserved capacity that covers sustained 2,500 qps and an eu vpc to keep traffic in region?
[01:22] Priya (BeaconForge): yes and also we need tighter audit logs and KMS control for the eu rollout — compliance team will want key separation.
[01:30] Diego: okay makes sense. quick clarifying Q: when you say KMS control, do you mean customer-managed keys in the VPC/HSM or just KMS integration for redwood-managed instances?
[01:42] Priya: customer-managed KMS, ideally HSM-backed.
[01:46] Diego: noted. we can support CMK with HSM via our private offering — there are a few configuration steps but we've done it with other customers.
[01:55] Elena (BeaconForge): one more thing — model quality. we ran a couple of evals on the latest quantized variant and saw slight regression on named-entity recall. need to understand fallback options if quality degrades after quant.
[02:08] Diego: good flag. our recommendation is canary with traffic slicing by user cohort and automatic fallback to the floating-hosted model if regression crosses threshold. we also have prompt-set based regression alerts in Optimize.
[02:20] Raj: ok that matches our risk appetite. what's the timeline for the eu VPC provisioning?
[02:26] Maya: from signed amendment to provision typically 2-3 weeks for EU VPC staging, but can compress to ~10 days with a prioritized ticket and provided network/docs are complete.
[02:36] Tom: what network artifacts do you need from us?
[02:39] Diego: we'll need CIDR ranges, peering contact, any firewall/NAT requirements, and if you want private link endpoints. we'll share a template.
[02:48] Raj: good. can you drop that template after the call?
[02:51] Maya: yes i'll send the network template and SOC2 + architecture diagram links after the call (deck + security pack).
[02:58] Elena: and the benchmark — can we run a throughput test against a staging cluster in eu? we want to validate 2,500 qps with p95 under 180ms for our prompt mix.
[03:09] Diego: absolutely. we'll set a benchmark window. depends on model variant — quantized runs can be denser so we need to pick kernel/quant profile. i'd recommend running both fp16 and 4-bit quant for comparison.
[03:21] Tom: is there an extra cost for the quantized variant vs fp16?
[03:25] Maya: cost delta depends on throughput and GPU type; Optimize can give estimated unit cost savings. pricing in the amendment will reflect the chosen profile and reserved capacity.
[03:33] Raj: one concern — what about failover? if eu capacity hits an incident can we fail back to hosted in us-east with encryption in transit?
[03:42] Diego: yes, we support policy-based routing: primary eu VPC with automatic fallback to a compatible model in hosted US region. latency will be higher, but you remain online and we keep telemetry to track degradation.
[03:52] Priya: for auditing, we'll need request-level logs for a rolling 90 days and searchability for investigations.
[03:58] Maya: we can set log retention and give RBAC access to specific identities. full audit exports are available as an add-on. i'll include options in the SOW.
[04:06] Elena: can you also surface token-level cost per route? we want to map which features are driving spend.
[04:12] Diego: yes, Console has token-breakdown by route and model; we'll include a sample report.
[04:17] Raj: ok let's talk numbers briefly. our finance team wants a 12-month committed uplift starting May 15: 2x baseline committed, plus ability to burst another 1.5x. what's the contractual path?
[04:29] Maya: we can do a reserved capacity amendment: committed baseline at discounted unit rates, and a burst bucket billed at on-demand rates. for burst above the reserved+burst we can tier pricing or offer pre-purchased burst credits. i'll put proposed bands in the draft SOW.
[04:41] Raj: and SLA? we need a formal p99 SLO for steady-state traffic ideally < 400ms for production, with credits for misses.
[04:50] Diego: we can include an SLA for dedicated clusters; for private VPC there's an operational dependency on network peering so SLA is conditioned on completed onboarding checklist. we'll state SLOs and credit structure in amendment.
[05:02] Tom: on the technical runbook — how do we handle warm starts and KV cache warming to reduce cold-start token latency?
[05:09] Diego: automatic prefix caching is supported — you can pin hot prompts to the cache during spin-up. for model warm-up we recommend a rolling warm pool to keep some workers hot; this is part of the dedicated provisioning strategy.
[05:22] Priya: what's the expected lead time to get 2,500 qps with those warm pools?
[05:27] Diego: depends on instance class; with our recommended cluster config we can handle sustained 2.5k qps within ~7-10 days of provisioning if the warm pool is sized appropriately.
[05:36] Raj: okay good. about the model variants — do you support pinned model versions so we can roll back if the new quantized model regresses?
[05:43] Maya: yes model pinning and versioned rollouts are built in; we also support canary percentages and automatic rollback on metric drift.
[05:50] Elena: we ran into an issue where tokenization changed between model versions and broke a small part of our pipeline — will you preserve tokenizer metadata during upgrades?
[05:59] Diego: good point. tokenizer/serialization metadata is preserved and we recommend a compatibility test in the staging cluster before cutover.
[06:07] Raj: nice. anything on compliance? our audit team will ask for SOC2 report, dataflow diagrams, and legal appendix on data residency.
[06:15] Maya: i'll attach SOC2 and a dataflow diagram. legal appendix is standard; i'll ask our legal to prepare the data residency clause for eu-only processing.
[06:24] Tom: and billing — do we have to set up a separate billing entity for EU consumption or can it roll into our existing account?
[06:31] Maya: usually it rolls into the same account but billing code can be broken out by region. if you need a separate invoicing entity that's possible but adds billing setup time.
[06:40] Raj: can you give an outline of the SOW milestones now so we can share internally?
[06:46] Maya: sure: 1) Sign amendment (target by 2026-03-26), 2) EU VPC network handoff + docs (3-5 days after sign), 3) Provisioning + staging cluster (7-10 days), 4) Benchmark window + acceptance (3 days), 5) Production cutover (per plan, targeting 2026-05-15).
[07:03] Priya: that timeline looks tight but doable if we move quickly on the network artifacts.
[07:08] Elena: for the benchmark, can Diego share the exact payload and tools you'll run so our infra team can mirror?
[07:14] Diego: yes i'll share the runbook and k6 config, and a link to the benchmark sheet — we'll run both gen and chat loads with your eval prompts.
[07:25] Raj: any blockers from redwood side?
[07:28] Maya: nothing major — just finalizing pricing bands and the SOW language.
[07:32] Tom: last Q: is there a difference in the incident response path for Dedicated vs Private VPC?
[07:38] Diego: incident ops are similar, but for Private VPC the first-line network checks are on your side; we coordinate via NOC and have a runbook that maps responsibilities. we'll include contact escalation matrix in the SOW.
[07:50] Raj: ok sounds good. let's lock the next steps.
[07:53] Maya: recap of next steps: i'll send pricing & SOW draft, SOC2 + network template; diego will prepare benchmark runbook and schedule; beaconforge will send traffic profile and confirm billing contact.
[07:59] Priya: agreed. can we put the benchmark week tentatively on April 5-9?
[08:04] Diego: tentatively yes i'll propose slots and share calendar invites. we might need a two-hour maintenance window for the staging tests.
[08:11] Elena: ok. also, please include an option for extended audit retention (90 vs 180 days) and export frequency.
[08:18] Maya: will do.
[08:20] Raj: thanks everyone — look forward to the SOW.
[08:23] Maya: thanks all, we'll follow up by EOD tomorrow with the doc links.

[08:30] (meeting wraps; total duration ~62 minutes)
